Mnemonic Cloze

fields: Why is Secure Score not a compliance score?
Secure Score measures adoption of Microsoft's own recommendations. Regulatory compliance in Defender for Cloud measures a named framework such as ISO 27001 or NIST SP 800-53.
Which service extends Defender for Servers to on-premises, AWS and GCP machines?
Azure Arc — it projects the server into Azure as a connected machine, which Defender for Cloud can then onboard.
NSG or ASG: which one groups VMs by role so rules refer to the group instead of IP ranges?
The application security group (ASG). The NSG holds the rules; the ASG is what those rules point at.
Which Microsoft Entra feature grants Global Administrator for a fixed window, with approval, instead of permanently?
Privileged Identity Management (PIM) — an eligible assignment the user activates.
A storage account must be reachable only from one VNet subnet. Storage firewall rule or private endpoint?

Both restrict access, but only the private endpoint gives the account a private IP in the subnet and lets you drop the public endpoint entirely. Firewall rules still allow traffic over the public endpoint.
In Microsoft Sentinel, {{c1::automation rules}} decide when a response runs, and {{c2::playbooks}} are the Logic Apps that carry it out.
Which Defender for Cloud capability scans resources and code for exposed secrets?
Defender CSPM secret scanning — agentless, it finds secrets on VM disks, in code repositories and in cloud deployments.
A Copilot Studio agent's identity is compromised. Which tool shows what that agent could reach?
Blast radius analysis in the Defender XDR incident graph — it maps paths from the compromised Entra Agent ID to critical assets.
Which diagnostic shows the security rules actually in force on a VM's network interface, after all NSGs are combined?
Azure Network Watcher effective security rules.
PIM: what separates an eligible assignment from an active one?
Active = the role is held right now. Eligible = the user must activate it, for a limited time and usually behind approval and MFA.
Which Microsoft Purview capability surfaces data that Microsoft Copilot could over-expose?
Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI.
Why does just-in-time VM access reduce risk rather than merely add friction?
A permanently open management port is scanned and brute-forced continuously. JIT shrinks the exposed window from always to a few minutes a week.
Azure SQL auditing can write its log to {{c1::a storage account}}, {{c2::Log Analytics}} or {{c3::Event Hubs}}.
Admins need occasional RDP to a VM, but the port must not stand open. Which Defender for Servers feature?
Just-in-time (JIT) VM access — the port opens for a bounded window after a request is approved.
Defender EASM or Defender CSPM: which finds internet-facing assets you did not know you owned?
Defender External Attack Surface Management (EASM). CSPM assesses the posture of assets already known to Azure.
Private endpoint or Private Link service: which is the consumer-side network interface inside your own VNet?
The private endpoint. Private Link service is the provider side — it publishes your service so others can reach it privately.
How does Microsoft Sentinel collect Windows Security events from servers?
The Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection rule (Windows Security Events via AMA). Machines that can't run the agent forward to a WEC server that does.
Azure Key Vault stores {{c1::keys}}, {{c2::secrets}} and {{c3::certificates}}.
Why prefer a managed identity over a service principal with a client secret?
There is no credential to store, rotate or leak — Azure owns the lifecycle. A leaked client secret is valid until someone notices.
An auditor wants proof that every Global Administrator still needs the role. Which PIM feature?
Access reviews on the role — reviewers confirm or remove each assignment, and denied ones can be removed automatically.
Activating an eligible role in PIM can require {{c1::MFA}}, {{c2::a justification}} and {{c3::approval}}.
Configured per role in the PIM role settings.
PIM: which kind of role covers Owner on an Azure subscription, Azure resource roles or Microsoft Entra roles?
Azure resource roles. Entra roles such as Global Administrator govern the directory, not Azure resources.
Why use PIM for Groups instead of eligible role assignments on each user?
One eligible group membership can carry several role assignments at once, so you govern one object instead of many.
What does a Conditional Access policy in report-only mode do?
It evaluates every sign-in and logs what it would have done, without enforcing anything — so you can measure impact before turning it on.
Admins must use phishing-resistant MFA, but other users may keep the Authenticator app. Which Conditional Access grant control?
Require authentication strength set to Phishing-resistant MFA, in a policy scoped to the admin roles.
Why exclude break-glass (emergency access) accounts from Conditional Access policies?
A broken policy can lock every admin out of the tenant; those accounts are the way back in. Alert on their sign-ins instead.
Entra ID Protection: is a leaked password found on the dark web a sign-in risk or a user risk?
User risk — the account itself is compromised. Sign-in risk is about one authentication looking suspicious, such as from an anonymous IP.
Sign-ins from countries you don't operate in must be blocked. Which Conditional Access building block do you need?
A named location of countries/regions used as a condition, with Block as the grant control.
What does Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) add to Conditional Access?
Supporting resources revoke tokens in near real time on critical events — user disabled, password reset, location change — instead of waiting for expiry.
Every agent identity that Entra ID Protection flags as high risk must be blocked. What do you build?
A Conditional Access policy targeting All agent identities, with the Agent risk condition set to High and the Block grant control.
Does a Conditional Access policy that targets All users also cover an agent's user account?
No. Agent user accounts and agent identities have to be targeted explicitly; user-targeted policies don't include them.
Why shouldn't agent identities rely on your existing "require MFA for all users" policy?
Agents can't complete interactive controls like MFA. They need dedicated policies built on identity filters, agent risk and locations.
How can one Conditional Access policy cover every agent created from the same template, including future ones?
Target the agent identity blueprint — the policy applies to every agent identity derived from it.
Conditional Access must apply to hundreds of agent identities by a business label such as Environment=Prod. What do you use?
Custom security attributes on the agent identities, selected in the policy's agent assignment.
FIDO2 security key or Authenticator push approval: which is phishing-resistant?
FIDO2 (and passkeys, Windows Hello for Business). The credential is bound to the real site's origin, so a fake sign-in page gets nothing usable. A push approval can be relayed.
Where in Microsoft Entra ID do you control which MFA and passwordless methods users may register?
The Authentication methods policy.
What attack does number matching in Microsoft Authenticator defend against?
MFA fatigue — the user must type the number shown on the sign-in screen, so blindly approving a stray push no longer works.
What is a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) for?
A time-limited passcode that lets a user sign in and register a passwordless method, without ever having a password.
App registration or enterprise application: which is the tenant-local object that holds user assignments and consent grants?
The enterprise application (service principal). The app registration is the app's global definition in its home tenant.
Delegated or application permission: which lets a background daemon read every mailbox with no user signed in?
Application permission — the app acts as itself and needs admin consent. Delegated permissions are capped by what the signed-in user can do.
Users keep consenting to unknown apps that read their mail. Which settings stop this but leave a path for legitimate requests?
Restrict user consent (for example, verified publishers and low-impact permissions only) and turn on the admin consent workflow so users can request approval.
Why doesn't resetting the user's password fix an illicit consent grant?
The attacker's app holds an OAuth grant and refresh tokens, not the password. You have to revoke the grant or remove the service principal.
Setting {{c1::Assignment required}} to Yes on an enterprise application means only assigned users and groups can get a token for it.
System-assigned or user-assigned managed identity: which survives deletion of the resource it is attached to?
User-assigned — it is a standalone Azure resource that several resources can share. A system-assigned identity is deleted with its resource.
Twenty VMs in a pool need identical Key Vault access. Which managed identity type fits?
One user-assigned managed identity attached to all of them — grant access once instead of twenty times.
Key Vault: Azure RBAC or vault access policies — which lets you grant access to a single secret?
Azure RBAC — role assignments can be scoped to one key, secret or certificate. Access policies apply to the whole vault.
Which built-in role lets an app read Key Vault secret values without managing the vault?
Key Vault Secrets User.
Why is Key Vault Contributor dangerous on a vault that uses the access-policy model?
It manages the vault, so it can write itself an access policy that grants data access. Under the Azure RBAC model that escalation path doesn't exist.
Key Vault soft delete or purge protection: which stops even an admin from permanently deleting a vault before retention ends?
Purge protection. Soft delete makes deleted items recoverable; purge protection blocks a forced purge during retention, and can't be turned off once on.
Key Vault soft-delete retention can be set from {{c1::7}} to {{c2::90}} days.
A Key Vault must accept traffic only from one VNet plus Azure services such as Backup. Which settings?
Key Vault firewall set to selected networks for that VNet, plus Allow trusted Microsoft services to bypass this firewall.
What does Microsoft Defender for Key Vault detect?
Unusual access to a vault — for example from a Tor exit node, by an unfamiliar app or user, or a sudden spike in secret reads.
TLS certificates stored in Key Vault keep expiring unnoticed. What should you configure on them?
A certificate lifetime action: auto-renew through an integrated CA, or email contacts at a set point before expiry.
Key Vault Premium or Managed HSM: which gives you a single-tenant HSM pool where you hold the security domain?
Managed HSM. Key Vault Premium protects keys in HSMs that are shared across tenants.
What does a Key Vault key rotation policy automate?
Creating a new key version on a schedule. Services that reference the versionless key URI pick up the new version automatically.
Azure Policy or Azure RBAC: which stops an Owner from deploying a VM in a disallowed region?
Azure Policy — it governs what resources may look like, whoever deploys them. RBAC only governs who may act.
The Azure Policy effect {{c1::Deny}} blocks a non-compliant request, while {{c2::Audit}} lets it through and flags it.
Azure Policy: DeployIfNotExists or Modify — which effect adds a missing tag to a resource?
Modify — it changes properties such as tags during create or update. DeployIfNotExists deploys a related resource, like a diagnostic setting.
Why do DeployIfNotExists and Modify policy assignments need a managed identity?
They deploy or change resources on your behalf, including during remediation, so the assignment needs its own identity holding the roles to do it.
Resources that existed before a DeployIfNotExists policy was assigned are non-compliant. How do you fix them?
Run a remediation task. On its own, the policy only acts on new create and update requests.
What is an Azure Policy initiative?
A set of policy definitions assigned and tracked as one unit — the Microsoft cloud security benchmark is one.
CanNotDelete or ReadOnly resource lock: which still lets you resize a VM?
CanNotDelete — it only blocks deletion. ReadOnly blocks every write, which can break operations such as listing storage account keys.
Why can a resource lock stop a subscription Owner?
Locks apply to every user and role, Owner included. The lock must be removed before the blocked operation will succeed.
Azure custom role or Entra custom role: which do you need to let operators restart VMs and nothing else?
An Azure custom role with the VM restart action. Entra custom roles cover directory objects such as app registrations, not Azure resources.
In an Azure custom role, {{c1::NotActions}} subtracts permissions from Actions — it is not a deny.
Another role assignment can still grant the same permission. Use Azure Policy to actually block something.
User Access Administrator or Owner: which can assign Azure roles but can't create resources?
User Access Administrator. Owner can do both.
Which Defender CSPM capability flags identities whose granted permissions far exceed what they use?
Permissions management (CIEM) — recommendations to remove unused or over-provisioned permissions across Azure, AWS and GCP.
Azure Backup {{c1::soft delete}} keeps deleted backup data recoverable for {{c2::14}} days by default.
Retention can be extended, and enhanced soft delete can be made always-on.
Azure Backup: immutable vault or multi-user authorization (MUA) — which needs a second person's approval through a Resource Guard?
MUA. An immutable vault blocks operations that would remove recovery points, and can be locked so it can't be disabled.
Why put the Resource Guard for Azure Backup MUA in a different subscription or tenant?
So the backup admin can't approve their own critical operation — the guard belongs to someone else, typically the security team.
Which Defender for Cloud capability scans IaC templates in your repos for misconfigurations before deployment?
DevOps security — connect GitHub, Azure DevOps or GitLab and it scans IaC in pipelines and pull requests.
Why enforce security settings in the IaC template rather than fixing the deployed resource?
A template fix is reviewed like code and applies to every future deployment. A fix on the live resource drifts and is overwritten on the next deploy.
How do you add ISO 27001 to the Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard?
Add the standard to the subscription under Environment settings → Security policies. Compliance standards need a paid plan such as Defender CSPM.
Which security standard does Defender for Cloud apply to every subscription by default?
The Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB).
A Defender for Cloud recommendation doesn't apply to a test subscription. How do you stop it counting against you?
Create an exemption (waiver or mitigated) for that scope. The resource stops affecting Secure Score.
Account SAS or user delegation SAS: which is signed with Entra credentials instead of the account key?
User delegation SAS — Microsoft's recommended kind. Account and service SAS are signed with the account key.
Why disable shared key authorization on a storage account?
Account keys grant full access outside Entra ID and RBAC. Turning them off forces identity-based, auditable access — and kills key-signed SAS tokens.
A service SAS must be revocable without rotating the storage account key. What should it be tied to?
A stored access policy on the container. Delete or change the policy and every SAS bound to it stops working.
The storage account setting {{c1::Allow Blob anonymous access}} must be off to stop anyone making a container public.
Storage Blob Data Reader or Reader: which lets a user read blob contents with Entra authentication?
Storage Blob Data Reader — a data-plane role. Reader is control-plane only: it sees the account, not the data.
What does "Secure transfer required" on a storage account enforce?
HTTPS for REST calls and encrypted SMB 3.x for Azure Files. Plain HTTP and unencrypted SMB are rejected.
Microsoft-managed keys or customer-managed keys: which lets you cut off Azure's ability to decrypt your storage data?
Customer-managed keys in Key Vault or Managed HSM. Disable or revoke the key and the data becomes unreadable.
What does infrastructure encryption add to Azure Storage?
A second layer of AES-256 encryption at the infrastructure level, with a separate key, under the normal service-level encryption.
Uploaded blobs must be checked for malware before an app processes them. Which Defender for Storage feature?
On-upload malware scanning. Results are written to blob index tags and can trigger alerts or automation.
What does Defender for Storage activity monitoring alert on?
Suspicious access patterns — access from Tor exit nodes, unusual data extraction, or anonymous access to sensitive containers.
Storage service endpoint or private endpoint: which still sends traffic to the account's public endpoint?
The service endpoint — traffic stays on the Azure backbone but targets the public endpoint. A private endpoint gives the account a private IP in your VNet.
What does a service endpoint policy add to a Storage service endpoint?
It limits which storage accounts the subnet may reach over the endpoint, which stops exfiltration to an attacker's own storage account.
A storage account firewall blocks Azure Backup from reaching the account. Which setting fixes it?
The exception Allow trusted Microsoft services, or a resource instance rule for that specific resource.
What does immutable (WORM) blob storage protect against?
Changing or deleting blobs during the retention interval or legal hold — even by the account owner.
Azure SQL: server-level or database-level firewall rule — which moves with the database during geo-replication?
Database-level rules — they are stored in the database itself. Server-level rules live in master.
Only Microsoft Entra identities may sign in to an Azure SQL logical server. What do you enable?
Microsoft Entra-only authentication — SQL authentication is turned off for the server.
TDE or Always Encrypted: which keeps data hidden even from the database engine and its admins?
Always Encrypted — the keys stay with the client app. TDE encrypts data at rest, but the engine decrypts it for anyone who can query.
Does Dynamic Data Masking in Azure SQL encrypt anything?
No. It masks column values in query results for non-privileged users. The stored data is unchanged.
Azure SQL auditing: server-level or database-level policy — which covers every database on the server, including new ones?
The server-level policy. A database-level policy adds to it; it doesn't replace it.
What does Defender for SQL vulnerability assessment check?
Misconfigurations and excessive permissions in the database, compared against a baseline you approve, with remediation scripts.
What kind of activity does Defender for Azure SQL threat protection alert on?
SQL injection, brute-force sign-in attempts, and access from unusual locations or principals.
Which Defender plan protects Azure Database for PostgreSQL and MySQL?
Defender for open-source relational databases. Azure SQL and SQL on machines have their own Defender for SQL plans.
Which Defender plan detects suspicious access to an Azure Cosmos DB account?
Defender for Azure Cosmos DB, one of the Defender for Databases plans.
NSG rules are processed in {{c1::priority}} order, lowest number first, and processing stops at the first match.
A subnet NSG allows inbound 443, but the VM's NIC NSG denies it. Does the traffic reach the VM?
No. Inbound traffic must pass the subnet NSG and then the NIC NSG, and both have to allow it.
Which default NSG rule lets VMs in peered VNets talk to each other?
AllowVnetInBound — the VirtualNetwork tag includes peered and connected address spaces.
Why use service tags in NSG rules instead of IP ranges?
Microsoft maintains the addresses behind a tag such as Storage or AzureCloud, so the rule stays correct as Azure's IP ranges change.
AVNM security admin rule: Allow or Always Allow — which still lets an NSG deny the traffic?
Allow. Always Allow and Deny end evaluation, so the NSG never sees that traffic.
Central IT must block inbound RDP from the internet on every VNet, and app teams must not be able to override it. Which feature?
An Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rule with Deny. It is evaluated before the NSGs that app teams control.
In Azure Virtual Network Manager, what decides which VNets a security admin configuration applies to?
Network groups — static membership, or dynamic membership through Azure Policy conditions.
Azure Firewall or NSG: which can filter outbound traffic by FQDN?
Azure Firewall. NSGs work only on IPs, ports and service tags.
Azure Firewall Standard or Premium: which adds TLS inspection and signature-based IDPS?
Premium. Standard filters by FQDN and threat intelligence, but can't decrypt traffic.
Azure Firewall processes {{c1::DNAT}} rules first, then {{c2::network}} rules, then {{c3::application}} rules.
Internet-bound traffic from spoke VNets must go through Azure Firewall in the hub. What do you configure?
A route table on the spoke subnets: 0.0.0.0/0 with the firewall's private IP as next hop.
What does Azure Firewall Manager add?
Central firewall policies, with parent–child inheritance, applied across many firewalls and secured virtual hubs.
What makes a Virtual WAN hub a secured virtual hub?
An Azure Firewall (or partner security provider) deployed in the hub and managed by Firewall Manager.
In Virtual WAN, branch-to-VNet traffic must be inspected by the hub firewall. Which feature?
Routing intent with a private traffic routing policy that points at the hub firewall.
Point-to-site VPN: which authentication type brings Conditional Access and MFA?
Microsoft Entra ID authentication (OpenVPN). Certificate and RADIUS authentication don't go through Entra Conditional Access.
What does a custom IPsec/IKE policy on an Azure VPN connection let you control?
The exact encryption and integrity algorithms and DH/PFS groups — to meet a compliance requirement or match an on-premises device.
Remote staff need on-premises file servers without a VPN, with Conditional Access per app. Which product?
Microsoft Entra Private Access: the Global Secure Access client on devices plus a private network connector on-premises.
Entra Private Access: Quick Access or per-app access — which is the least-privilege end state?
Per-app access. Quick Access publishes broad network ranges to replace a VPN fast, and is meant as a bridge.
Which component must run on-premises for Microsoft Entra Private Access to reach internal resources?
A Microsoft Entra private network connector, in a connector group with line of sight to the resources.
Why does a private endpoint usually need a private DNS zone such as privatelink.blob.core.windows.net?
Clients still use the service's normal name. The private zone makes that name resolve to the private endpoint's IP instead of the public one.
Your SaaS runs behind a Standard Load Balancer, and customers want to reach it privately from their own VNets. What do you create?
A Private Link service on the load balancer. Customers then create private endpoints that connect to it.
Does an NSG on a private endpoint's subnet filter traffic to the endpoint by default?
No. Network policies for private endpoints are off by default; enable them on the subnet for NSGs and route tables to apply.
Network Watcher: IP flow verify or effective security rules — which names the rule that allows or denies one specific packet?
IP flow verify — you test a 5-tuple and it reports the matching rule. Effective security rules shows the whole combined rule set.
Which Network Watcher feature replaces NSG flow logs?
Virtual network flow logs.
DDoS Network Protection or the free default infrastructure protection: which gives you attack telemetry, alerts and access to Microsoft's rapid response team?
DDoS Network Protection. The free default protects Azure's platform as a whole and isn't tuned to your application.
Before rolling out Copilot, you need to find SharePoint sites shared with "Everyone except external users". Which tool?
SharePoint Advanced Management data access governance (DAG) reports.
Restricted Content Discovery or Restricted Access Control: which hides a site from Copilot and org-wide search but leaves permissions unchanged?
Restricted Content Discovery. Restricted Access Control limits who can open the site at all, to members of chosen groups.
Owners of overshared SharePoint sites should fix their own permissions. Which SharePoint Advanced Management feature asks them to?
Site access review, started from a data access governance report.
What does Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI assess automatically every week?
The top 100 SharePoint sites by usage — a data risk assessment that flags content Copilot could overshare.
Users must be stopped from pasting sensitive data into third-party AI sites in Edge. What is the quickest start?
A DSPM for AI one-click policy, which creates a Purview DLP policy that blocks sensitive info being sent to AI apps in Edge.
Why must devices be onboarded to Purview before DSPM for AI can see ChatGPT usage?
Those prompts happen in the browser. Purview sees them only through endpoint DLP on onboarded devices (plus the browser extension).
At what moment does Defender real-time protection inspect a Copilot Studio agent?
Each time the agent is about to invoke a tool. Defender returns allow or block before the tool runs.
You turned on Copilot Studio real-time protection in the Defender portal, but nothing is blocked yet. Who else has to act?
A Power Platform administrator, who completes onboarding in Power Platform with the same Entra app ID.
What does the default real-time protection rule for cloud AI agents do in Microsoft Defender?
It only audits: matching activity is recorded as a behavior without being stopped. Blocking needs a custom rule.
Defender for AI Services or Foundry guardrails: which raises SOC alerts about jailbreak attempts on your model deployment?
Defender for AI Services in Defender for Cloud. Guardrails filter the content; Defender turns detections into security alerts.
What does prompt evidence add to Defender for AI Services alerts?
The suspicious part of the prompt or response, so the analyst can see exactly what triggered the alert.
Prompt Shields: user prompt attack or document attack — which catches instructions hidden in an email the agent reads?
Document attack (indirect prompt injection). User prompt attacks come from the user's own input.
Which Prompt Shields detection is off by default in Foundry guardrails?
Document attack detection — you have to enable it. User prompt attack detection is on by default.
A Foundry model deployment and the agent that uses it have different guardrails. Which one applies?
The agent's guardrail — it overrides the model's.
What does the Task adherence guardrail in Foundry detect?
An agent drifting from its assigned task — for example, tool calls that don't match what the user asked for.
Several teams share one model deployment and one team keeps exhausting its TPM quota. What do you put in front of it?
An AI gateway in API Management with the llm-token-limit policy, keyed per team or subscription.
Through a Foundry AI Gateway, exceeding the TPM limit returns HTTP {{c1::429}}, and exhausting the total token quota returns HTTP {{c2::403}}.
At what scope does the Foundry AI Gateway enforce token limits?
Per project — each project on the shared gateway gets its own TPM limit and quota.
What does the Data and AI security dashboard in Defender for Cloud show?
Data and AI resources in one place: protection coverage, sensitive data findings, internet exposure, and the top alerts, recommendations and attack paths.
Why does the Data and AI security dashboard need Defender CSPM with sensitive data discovery turned on?
Without it Defender can't tell which stores hold sensitive data, so it can't rank exposure by what is actually at risk.
What does Microsoft Entra Agent ID give an AI agent?
Its own identity in Entra, so Conditional Access, ID Protection and identity governance apply to the agent as they do to users.
Agents created by people who have since left the company have no accountable person. Which Entra Agent ID governance control prevents that?
Required sponsors and owners for every agent identity, with access granted through time-bound access packages.
Where do you block an agent for the whole organization in Microsoft 365?
Microsoft 365 admin center → Agents → All agents → Block. Blocking also turns off every instance of the agent.
How does the Microsoft 365 admin center surface shared agents whose creator was deleted?
An Agents without owners count and filter in the agent registry. From there you assign an owner, block or delete.
Azure Disk Encryption or encryption at host: which covers temp disks and caches without BitLocker or dm-crypt in the guest?
Encryption at host — encryption happens on the VM host. ADE runs BitLocker/dm-crypt in the guest OS and is being retired.
Server-side encryption of managed disks with customer-managed keys is configured through which resource?
A disk encryption set, which points at the key in Key Vault or Managed HSM.
Azure Bastion Basic or Standard: which supports native-client RDP/SSH connections?
Standard (and Premium). Basic supports connections through the browser only.
Why does Azure Bastion let you remove public IPs from VMs?
Users connect to Bastion over TLS, and Bastion reaches the VM's private IP. RDP and SSH are never exposed to the internet.
Azure Bastion must be deployed in a subnet named {{c1::AzureBastionSubnet}} of at least /26.
What does just-in-time VM access change when it opens a port?
It adds a temporary allow rule to the NSG (and Azure Firewall, if present) for the requester's IP, then removes it when time runs out.
Which Defender for Servers plan includes just-in-time VM access?
Plan 2.
Defender for Servers Plan 1 or Plan 2: which includes agentless scanning and file integrity monitoring?
Plan 2. Plan 1 is mainly Defender for Endpoint EDR plus agent-based vulnerability assessment.
How does agentless scanning in Defender for Servers inspect a VM?
It snapshots the disks and scans them out of band for vulnerabilities, software inventory, secrets and malware — no agent, no load on the VM.
An on-premises server was onboarded by installing Defender for Endpoint directly instead of through Azure Arc. What do you lose?
Most Plan 2 features — you get Plan 1 plus premium vulnerability management only. Onboard through Arc for full coverage.
How are AWS EC2 instances onboarded to Defender for Servers by default?
Connecting the AWS account to Defender for Cloud onboards its machines as Azure Arc-enabled servers.
What does file integrity monitoring in Defender for Servers watch for?
Changes to OS files, registry keys and application files that could indicate an attack.
Trusted launch or confidential VM: which encrypts VM memory so even the host can't read it?
Confidential VM. Trusted launch protects the boot chain with secure boot and vTPM, not memory.
Trusted launch combines {{c1::secure boot}}, {{c2::a virtual TPM (vTPM)}} and {{c3::boot integrity monitoring}}.
Set by choosing the Trusted launch security type when you create the VM.
Why does secure boot defeat a bootkit?
Only boot components signed by trusted publishers load, so a bootloader patched by malware refuses to start.
What does Azure Machine Configuration (formerly Guest Configuration) do?
Audits or applies settings inside the OS of Azure and Arc machines through Azure Policy — password rules, installed software, and so on.
Why does Azure Machine Configuration need the VM to have a managed identity?
The extension uses it to download configuration packages and report compliance back to Azure.
What does Defender for Containers protect?
Kubernetes clusters (AKS, EKS, GKE, Arc-enabled) at runtime, plus vulnerability assessment of container images in registries.
AKS: Azure RBAC or Kubernetes RBAC for authorization — which lets you grant cluster access with Azure role assignments?
Azure RBAC for Kubernetes authorization. With Kubernetes RBAC you write Role and RoleBinding objects inside the cluster.
An AKS API server must not be reachable from the internet at all. Which option?
A private cluster — the API server gets a private IP in your VNet. Authorized IP ranges only restrict the public endpoint.
Why disable local accounts on an AKS cluster?
The local cluster-admin credential bypasses Entra ID, so it escapes Conditional Access, MFA and per-user audit.
What does Microsoft Entra Workload ID do for AKS pods?
A pod exchanges its Kubernetes service account token for an Entra token, so it reaches Azure resources without stored secrets.
ACR admin user or a managed identity with AcrPull: which should AKS use to pull images?
AcrPull on the cluster's kubelet managed identity. The admin user is a single shared credential that can also push.
Which Azure Container Registry tier do you need for private endpoints?
Premium.
A Container Apps workload must be reachable only from your VNet. What do you configure?
A Container Apps environment in your VNet with internal ingress, so there's no public endpoint.
Entra sign-in must protect an Azure Functions HTTP API without code changes. Which feature?
App Service authentication (Easy Auth) with the Microsoft identity provider.
Function access key or Easy Auth: which actually proves who the caller is?
Easy Auth with Entra ID. A function key is a shared secret, and anyone holding it gets in.
App Service and Functions: VNet integration or private endpoint — which controls inbound access to the app?
The private endpoint. VNet integration only routes the app's outbound traffic into your VNet.
An App Service app should accept traffic only from your Azure Front Door profile. How?
An access restriction allowing the AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag, plus a header check on X-Azure-FDID for your Front Door ID.
Why isn't the URL of a Logic App HTTP trigger enough protection by itself?
The URL carries a SAS signature, so anyone who has it can fire the workflow. Restrict caller IPs or require Entra OAuth as well.
WAF on Application Gateway or on Front Door: which inspects traffic at Microsoft's global edge before it reaches your region?
Front Door WAF. Application Gateway WAF is regional and sits in your VNet.
WAF Detection or Prevention mode: which blocks a request that matches a rule?
Prevention. Detection only logs — start there to tune out false positives.
In Azure WAF, {{c1::custom rules}} are evaluated before the managed rule set.
Use them for geo-filtering, IP allow/deny lists and rate limits.
API Management must reject requests that lack a valid Entra-issued token before calling the back end. Which policy?
validate-jwt (or validate-azure-ad-token).
Which API Management policy throttles each client separately, by IP or subscription?
rate-limit-by-key.
Why should API Management call the back end with its managed identity?
The back end then trusts only APIM's identity, and no credential sits in the APIM policy.
{{c1::Attack path analysis}} in Defender CSPM shows how an attacker could chain weaknesses to reach a critical asset.
Cloud security explorer or attack path analysis: which do you use to ask your own question, such as "internet-exposed VMs with a high-severity CVE"?
Cloud security explorer — you build the graph query. Attack paths are precomputed by Defender.
What does a Defender for Cloud governance rule do?
Assigns an owner and a due date to matching recommendations automatically, so remediation is tracked.
Defender for Cloud must assess an AWS account. What do you create?
An AWS connector under Environment settings. It deploys a CloudFormation template that grants Defender the roles it needs.
What does Defender for Resource Manager detect?
Suspicious management operations on Azure — calls from malicious IPs, or use of exploitation toolkits against your subscription.
Which engine provides vulnerability assessment for Azure VMs in Defender for Servers?
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, turned on by default through the Defender for Endpoint integration.
Some VMs can't run the Defender for Endpoint agent, but you still need their vulnerability findings. What do you turn on?
Agentless scanning, in Defender for Servers Plan 2 or Defender CSPM.
How does Defender EASM discover assets you didn't know you owned?
From seeds you give it (domains, IP blocks, ASNs), it keeps following connections such as DNS, WHOIS and certificates.
When is a second Microsoft Sentinel workspace justified?
Data residency or sovereignty, billing separation, or strict access separation such as between subsidiaries. Otherwise use one workspace with table-level or resource-context RBAC.
Which Microsoft Sentinel role lets an analyst manage incidents but not create analytics rules?
Microsoft Sentinel Responder.
Which role does Sentinel itself need on a playbook's resource group before automation rules can run that playbook?
Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor.
The {{c1::Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator}} role lets a user run playbooks manually without being able to edit them.
What does a Microsoft Sentinel content hub solution package together?
Connectors, analytics rules, workbooks, hunting queries, parsers and playbooks for one product or scenario, installed and updated as a unit.
Sentinel needs Azure Activity logs from every subscription. How does the connector apply at scale?
The Azure Activity connector uses an Azure Policy assignment to create a diagnostic setting on each subscription.
How do CEF messages from a firewall appliance reach Microsoft Sentinel?
The appliance sends them to a Linux log forwarder running the Azure Monitor Agent, and a data collection rule sends them to the CommonSecurityLog table.
Syslog via AMA or CEF via AMA: which lands in the CommonSecurityLog table?
CEF via AMA. Plain Syslog lands in the Syslog table.
Why must a CEF source not also be collected by a Syslog DCR on the same facility?
The events are ingested twice — into Syslog and into CommonSecurityLog — so you pay double and get duplicates.
Sentinel: Windows Security Events via AMA or Windows Forwarded Events — which writes to the SecurityEvent table?
Windows Security Events via AMA. Forwarded Events writes to WindowsEvent, so built-in rules that query SecurityEvent won't match it.
What must run on the Windows Event Collector (WEC) server for the Windows Forwarded Events connector?
The Azure Monitor Agent, collecting the Forwarded Events channel through a data collection rule.
What does an on-premises Windows server need before the Azure Monitor Agent can collect from it?
Azure Arc — the agent needs the server to exist as an Azure resource.
You want only logon events 4624 and 4625 from Windows servers, to save ingestion cost. What do you configure?
A custom XPath query in the data collection rule.
Which API sends custom application data into a Sentinel custom (_CL) table?
The Logs Ingestion API, through a data collection rule that maps and transforms the data into the table.
What does an ingestion-time transformation in a data collection rule let you do?
Filter or reshape rows with KQL before they're stored — drop noisy events, strip PII, or route data to another table.
Every incident from one analytics rule must be assigned to the network team and tagged, without a Logic App. Which feature?
An automation rule — it can assign owners, add tags, and change status or severity on its own.
Why should a Sentinel playbook authenticate with a managed identity?
The Logic App gets only the roles it needs, such as Microsoft Sentinel Responder, and no credential is stored in its connections.
Enabling Microsoft Sentinel on a workspace includes free retention for the first {{c1::90}} days.
Longer analytics-tier retention, and data lake retention, are billed.
Sentinel analytics tier or data lake tier: which should hold high-volume firewall logs you only need for forensics?
The data lake tier — cheap long-term storage queried with KQL jobs, but no real-time analytics rules.
Total retention in the Microsoft Sentinel data lake can be extended to up to {{c1::12}} years.
What happens if you shorten a Sentinel table's total retention by mistake?
Microsoft waits 30 days before deleting the data, so you can revert the change.
Which Defender XDR advanced hunting table holds Microsoft 365 audit activity from SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange?
CloudAppEvents.
Where can you search the Purview unified audit log without leaving the Defender portal?
The Audit page in the Microsoft Defender portal.
Security Copilot owner or contributor: which can change which preinstalled plugins are available to the tenant?
Owner. Contributors create sessions and run promptbooks, but can't manage plugin availability or capacity.
Why doesn't the Copilot contributor role by itself show an analyst Sentinel incidents in Security Copilot?
Security Copilot acts on behalf of the user. The user also needs a Sentinel role, such as Microsoft Sentinel Reader, for the plugin to return data.
What do you purchase to give Security Copilot capacity?
Security compute units (SCUs), provisioned as an Azure resource.
Analysts need Security Copilot access, but must not be made Security Administrator. What do you assign?
A security group added to the Copilot contributor role in Security Copilot role assignment.
By default, who can add custom plugins in Security Copilot?
Only owners. An owner can let contributors add plugins for themselves, or for everyone.
What is a Security Copilot promptbook?
A saved sequence of prompts that runs as one workflow — for example, an incident summary followed by recommended actions.
Partner-built Security Copilot agents are acquired through the {{c1::Microsoft Security Store}}.
